_comment: The old behaviour, as exactly as the planner can still reproduce it.
Design 2026-10-20-point-count-reduction-design.md, section 5 and constraint C4.
scanplan plan --station input/station.json --config configs/legacy_exhaust.json --out output/legacy
Every switch that the point-count work turned on is turned back off here:
coverage_target_pct          null    greedy runs until nothing new is covered
cost_model                   millimetres   the upstream design's pricing
connector_level              2       retract + re-orient point between sweeps
order_axis_weight_mm_per_deg 0       order by distance alone
max_prune_rounds             8       the old round limit
Two differences cannot be switched off, and they are deliberate:
1. The selection score is gain / max(cost, eps) instead of gain / (cost + 1). The +1 was
one millimetre, so at millimetre pricing this is a 0.1% difference - but it is a
difference, and two candidates that scored within a tenth of a percent of each other
can now come out in the other order.
2. A selected pose is delivered as a zero-length stroke, so it appears in the path with
its own connectors instead of being counted in the coverage and then dropped from the
program.
Measured baseline to compare against (2026-10-20, upper face): the old code delivered 114
points and reported 99.741%, while the delivered strokes actually swept 91.98%. This profile
measured on the same part delivers 405 points at 99.74% and sweeps 99.75% - the difference is
97 selected poses (plus 194 connector points) that the old code counted in the coverage but
never wrote into the program. That is the accounting bug being fixed, not a regression, and it
can only ever ADD points to the delivery.
It also turns up 12 connector violations that the old program could not have shown, because
those connections did not exist in it: 5 routes keep negative clearance, 7 cannot spread a
90-136 deg flip over the largest lift within max_rot_deg_per_mm. That is why scenario 'deliver
every chosen item' and scenario 'price the choice in corners and order it by pose' are not
alternatives: the second is what makes the first survive a clearance check.
